item.title: Lake Hartwell Shoreline Cleanup: Drought exposes long-hidden trash; volunteers pull record 36 tires
item.description: In a remarkable display of community spirit, volunteers have gathered over 8,300 pounds of litter from the shores of Lake Hartwell, driven by an ongoing drought that has unveiled hidden debris. Amid concerns regarding the Clemson Lower Diversion Dam Saddle Dike, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has enforced specific restrictions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Chang’e-6 soil reveals metallic iron in lunar samples; it may preserve clues to Moon’s lost magnetic field
item.description: Recent analysis of lunar soil samples returned by China's Chang’e-6 mission revealed a unique form of iron. This iron, γ-Fe, exhibits exceptional magnetic properties, which could provide insights into the Moon's ancient magnetic field. Researchers suggest that extreme impacts on the lunar surface caused the formation and preservation of this unusual iron. The findings could enhance our understanding of the Moon's geological history and its evolution over time.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New dating rewrites history of Oklahoma meteor crater
item.description: Researchers from the University of Texas at Austin have traced the Ames meteor impact to approximately 370 million years ago, presenting a significant revision to the previously accepted estimate of 467 million years. This research connects the impact with the Frasnian-Famennian mass extinction event, employing zircon crystals to establish a more precise timeline, thus providing deeper insights into pivotal moments in Earth's geological history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Maryland manure-lagoon overflow kills nearly 11,000 fish across 25 species, officials say
item.description: A tragic incident has unfolded at Basin Run, where nearly 11,000 fish have succumbed to the consequences of a manure lagoon overflow from Kilby Farms. The Maryland Department of the Environment has traced the source of this discharge back to a series of ongoing pollution violations. Local residents, frustrated with the recurring environmental harm, are demanding accountability.

item.title: Scientists found a new magnetic mineral in Chang’e-6 Moon samples, preserved inside impact-glass particles
item.description: A groundbreaking discovery by researchers has unveiled a new magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, found in lunar samples from the Chang'e-6 mission. This remarkable find sheds light on the ancient magnetic environment of the Moon, now long lost. Detailed analysis of tiny iron particles within lunar impact glasses reveals that γ-Fe can maintain stable magnetic signals, potentially serving as a record of the Moon's magnetic history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: California schoolgirl's sewing project grows into nonprofit with 5,000+ care bags for women
item.description: Khloe Thompson, a California teenager, started making care bags for women in need after seeing homelessness. She founded the nonprofit Khloe Kares, which has distributed over 5,000 handmade bags containing personal-care items. The organization collaborates with local businesses and community groups to expand its outreach efforts. Thompson's initiatives have also included supporting children in Ghana and youth workshops on various topics. She received the George H.W.

item.title: Miami Beach’s historic Savoy Hotel could face demolition for a 38-story tower
item.description: Plans have been submitted to demolish much of the historic Savoy Hotel to construct a new 38-story tower. This project will utilize Florida's Live Local Act to overcome local zoning regulations and historic preservation concerns. The developer aims to retain a small section of the Savoy's facade and lobby in a nod to history. Local officials and preservationists have expressed strong opposition due to potential loss of cultural heritage.

item.title: Lithuania ready to cover cost if US establishes military base
item.description: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius has declared his willingness to finance the establishment of a permanent US military base in Lithuania. Since 2019, Lithuania has been hosting a rotating US battalion and is eager for a long-term military presence. Concurrently, the Lithuanian parliament is considering lifting constitutional prohibitions on nuclear weapons, a move that has drawn sharp criticism from Russia, citing heightened regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 150 years, 6 generations and 650 protected acres: The story of a Colorado ranch
item.description: Hutchinson Ranch, the oldest family-owned ranch in Colorado’s Upper Arkansas Valley, spans 700 acres along Highway 50. The Hutchinson family has maintained ownership for six generations, successfully implementing conservation agreements protecting 650 acres. These agreements prevent the land from being subdivided for development while allowing the family to continue ranching. Notable historic recognition occurred in 2003 when the ranch was identified among the top endangered properties in Colorado.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pak, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agree to deploy forces in Gulf country amid Houthi attacks
item.description: Pakistan and Turkiye have agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia following regional security threats from Houthi rebels. Representatives from the three countries held an emergency meeting to reinforce their Mecca defense agreement. This agreement establishes collective defense provisions that aim for a rapid military deployment if any country is attacked. Additionally, the committee appointed a retired Pakistani General as secretary-general to oversee defense strategies.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: In 2014, a Tennessee couple paid 58 cents for Vince Lombardi’s sweater; it later sold for $43,020
item.description: In an incredible find, a couple bought a sweater for just 58 cents at a Goodwill store in North Carolina back in 2014. While viewing a documentary, they learned that it had ties to famed football coach Vince Lombardi, as a tag revealed its association with his tenure at West Point. Eventually, it fetched an astonishing $43,020 at auction after being consigned by Lombardi's colleague's widow.
item.dc:creator: TOI Sports Desk

item.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger donated $250,000 for shelters for homeless veterans before Christmas
item.description: In 2021, Arnold Schwarzenegger donated $250,000 to Village for Vets to help provide temporary shelters for homeless veterans in Los Angeles. Before Christmas, 25 tiny shelters were installed at the VA campus in West Los Angeles. Each provided a bed, climate control, electricity and a locking door, giving veterans who had been living on the streets a safer place to stay while moving towards stable housing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida couple saves colorful Sarasota cottage village housing 17 small businesses from demolition
item.description: The anticipated transfer of the Historic Downtown Village in Sarasota to a developer has been called off. The cottages, which accommodate various local enterprises, will remain in the care of Alex and Marlene Lancaster. While business owners faced uncertainty regarding relocation and the emotional fallout of potential displacement, they now breathe a sigh of relief.

item.title: Patrick Swayze’s former California ranch with a dance studio listed for $4.5 million after $2.9 million sale
item.description: Rancho Bizarro, an extraordinary estate crafted by the artistic duo Patrick Swayze and Lisa Niemi, has hit the market once again. This idyllic ranch boasts state-of-the-art equestrian amenities, a vibrant dance studio, and a cozy main residence. After its acquisition by Aileen Getty in 2015 for $2.9 million, it is now available for $4.5 million.

item.title: George Lucas’ sprawling Skywalker Ranch in California
item.description: Nestled in Marin County, Skywalker Ranch is a vast 4,700-acre creative sanctuary brought to life by filmmaker George Lucas. This enchanting retreat features a Victorian-style main house used for professional gatherings and boasts Skywalker Sound, operating since 1987. With amenities like themed guest rooms, diverse dining options, and a health club, the ranch remains a unique filmmaking destination, nearly fifty years after its inception.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: From hunted-out woods to a deer refuge: How a Missouri couple transformed their 300-acre property
item.description: Mike and Dana Blevins turned their 300-acre property in Missouri into a thriving habitat for white-tailed deer. After purchasing the land, they implemented habitat management practices supported by the Missouri Department of Conservation. Their efforts contributed to the significant recovery of deer populations in the region, which faced near extinction in the past. As chronic wasting disease poses new challenges, they took part in management efforts to control infections.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wisconsin bargain hunter paid $29 for painting; later identified as Heade, sold for $882,500
item.description: In a remarkable turn of events, a man from Wisconsin stumbled upon a magnolia painting for just $29 at a rummage sale in the 1990s. A decade later, the artwork was authenticated as the work of esteemed American artist Martin Johnson Heade. Auctioned at Christie’s, it fetched an astonishing $882,500, shattering initial estimates of $300,000 to $500,000.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
